newsitem.title: USA: US, Britain, Japan to cooperate on futures trading.
newsitem.headline: US, Britain, Japan to cooperate on futures trading.

text.p: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said Thursday it had agreed with the Japanese Ministry of International Trade and Industry and the British Securities Investments Board to cooperate further on futures supervision.
Discussions between the three countries stemmed from recent events in the copper market, including trading losses by Sumitomo Corp, the CFTC said in a statement.
The three authorities aimed to "develop further their arrangements for international cooperation in the effective supervision of commodity futures markets," the statement said.
They will increase the exchange of information and co-sponsor a discussion of the issues, inviting countries that have commodity futures markets to participate, the CFTC said.
"We welcome this opportunity for regulatory authorities to further international cooperative efforts at market supervision," CFTC chair Brooksley Born said in the statement.
The nearly $2 billion copper trading loss by Sumitomo had focused the attention of international authorities on supervisiory issued raised by physical delivery markets, Born said.
Detailed arrangements for the planned discussion forum will be settled shortly, the CFTC said.
